subject: MAP & eval plan — pricing milestones, ramp, and contract redlines
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechco.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-06-08T14:12:00Z
Subject: MAP & eval timeline for POC

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers and quantization approach look promising. Our product and infra leads want to run a 6-week evaluation to validate cost and tail-latency under typical volume. Can you send a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a one-page eval plan with milestones tied to pricing/commits? Procurement also wants to understand how "usage" is defined for billing and whether there is price protection during model upgrades.

We have a hard goal to decide by July 10th so we can include this in our Q3 budget.

Attached: rough schedule from our side (Procurement).

Best,
Olivia
Olivia Barnes
Head of Product, FintechCo

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechco.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-09T09:24:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP & eval timeline for POC

Hi Olivia — really appreciate the clear timeline. Drafted a concise MAP and an eval plan and attached both; summary below.

High-level MAP (attached):
- Week 0: Account kickoff and credentialing (VPC/keys if private)
- Weeks 1–3: Integration + smoke tests; sample workloads for cost profiling
- Weeks 4–6: Load validation, tail-latency/quota tests; ramp to target concurrency
- Decision milestone (by 2026-07-10): commit level recommendation + pricing band

Commercial anchors we propose to tie to MAP milestones:
- Implementation milestone (end of week 3): 20% committed monthly units for Q3 pricing band
- Ramp milestone (end of week 6): commit increase to target monthly units (true-up applies for overshoot)
- Early-sign discount: 10% on committed units if contract signed within 7 days of decision milestone

Two clarifications up front that often come up: definition of usage (tokens vs. inference units) and true-up cadence. We propose billing on token-equivalent units with a quarterly true-up to reconcile committed vs. actual usage. Rafael — want to flag any legal/price-protection constraints we should avoid before I send the MAP to Fintech?

Olivia — attaching: FintechCo_MAP_v1.xlsx and a 1-page eval plan. If you want, we can lock a short call tomorrow to walk through the milestones and expected outputs per week.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
--- Attachments: FintechCo_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx); Redwood_EvalPlan_1pager.pdf (pdf) ---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-10T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP & eval timeline for POC - legal flags

Team — quick read of the MAP and proposed billing language. A few redline items to raise before we share: 

1) True-up cadence: Quarterly is fine, but we should explicitly state that refunds are not issued for under-usage; unutilized committed units roll forward for one quarter only. This avoids perpetual liability.

2) Price protection: Fintech is likely to ask for a price-protection clause during model upgrades. We can offer price protection for "equivalent model variants" for 12 months post-signing, but we must carve out material changes (architectural rewrites, model family changes) and any third-party licensing cost increases. Suggest concrete language for "equivalent" to be: same model family + within +/-20% cost profile.

3) Definition of usage: The contract should define billable units as "inference units (IU)" with the conversion table appended (tokens -> IU) and explicit mention that embeddings and reranking are measured differently. Avoid vague "API calls" definitions.

4) Credit triggers: We should avoid open-ended SLA credits tied to downstream business impact. Keep credits tied to measurable per-request latency or availability SLOs.

I'm attaching a marked-up SOW and a draft clause for price protection. Lauren — can you check procurement-side concessions (early-sign discount / ramp credits) against our standard commercial playbook?

-Rafael
Legal, Redwood Inference
--- Attachment: Redwood_Draft_SOW_Markup.pdf (pdf) ---

From: Andres Soto <asoto@fintechco.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechco.com>, procurement@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-06-12T11:42:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP & eval timeline for POC - legal flags (FintechCo redlines)

Soojin / Rafael — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached are FintechCo's redlines to the SOW and a separate memo on the "usage" definition. High level:

- We need a 90-day price-protection window from signature that covers any upgrades we adopt within the same model family. The 12-month protection you propose would be difficult for budgeting on our side.
- The definition of "equivalent model variants" must be operationalized. We propose: "same architecture and same tokenization with performance delta <= 10% on our standard benchmarks."
- On true-ups: Fintech requests a monthly reconciliation for committed vs. actual (not quarterly) with a 30-day invoice for shortfalls or overages.
- Early-sign discount: procurement would like that to be refundable as a credit if we don't reach the ramp milestone by the end of week 6.

We've attached a redlined document: FintechCo_SLA_Redline.docx and a short memo from procurement setting the decision deadline and approvals chain. Can we get Redwood's final position on cadence (monthly vs quarterly true-up) and the 90-day protection by EOD Friday (2026-06-12) so procurement can complete internal approvals?

Best,
Andres Soto
General Counsel, FintechCo
--- Attachments: FintechCo_SLA_Redline.docx (docx) ---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Andres Soto <asoto@fintechco.com>, Olivia Barnes <olivia@fintechco.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP & eval timeline for POC - legal flags (proposal)

Andres / Olivia — appreciate the clarity and the redlines. Quick summary and compromise proposal so we can hit your July 10 decision deadline: 

1) True-up cadence: We will accept monthly reconciliation for the POC period (Weeks 1–12) with settlement invoices due net 30. After the POC/contract effective date, cadence reverts to quarterly true-ups for committed annual agreements.

2) Price protection: We can do a 90-day price-protection window from signature that covers upgrades where the model remains in the same family and where cost delta is <= 15% on our internal cost metric. We will exclude third-party license changes and material architecture swaps. Rafael will provide exact clause language by EOD Monday.

3) Early-sign discount / ramp credit: We propose the 10% early-sign discount to apply to committed units at signing. If Fintech does not reach the ramp milestone by the end of Week 6, Redwood will convert the unused portion into a one-time credit that can be applied to the next quarter's committed units (valid for one quarter). This avoids refunds but gives procurement budget protection.

4) Usage definition: We'll attach a token->IU conversion table and a short appendix that separates generation, embeddings, and reranking metrics. This will be binding for the POC.

Next steps:
- Rafael to circulate final redline language for price protection and true-up by 2026-06-15EOD.
- Soojin to push updated MAP + SOW after Rafael's clauses; propose a 30-minute call 2026-06-16 to sign off and confirm procurement's DocuSign timeline.

If Fintech is good with this path, we'll convert an updated MAP into a DocuSign envelope and aim to have signature within 7 days of your decision milestone to lock the early-sign discount.

Thanks — talk soon.
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
